name: MC1455BDR2G
title: MC1455, MC1455B, NCV1455B: bipolar 555-type timer
summary: A single bipolar timer of the 555 kind, offered as a direct replacement for the NE555. One resistor and one capacitor set a one-shot delay; two resistors and one capacitor set the frequency and duty cycle of an oscillator. Separate trigger and reset inputs act on falling edges, and the output sources or sinks up to 200 mA. Three grades differ in temperature range: MC1455 (0 °C to 70 °C), MC1455B (-40 °C to 85 °C) and NCV1455B (-40 °C to 125 °C, automotive). MC1455BDR2G is the MC1455B in SOIC-8 on tape and reel, Pb-free.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 16 V operating; 18 V maximum

circuits.title: 22 second solid-state time-delay relay
circuits.description: A mains load switched by a triac after a fixed delay. The timer runs from a -10 V rail made from the 117 Vac line: the 1N4003 half-wave rectifies into the 10 µF capacitor and the 1N4740 zener, fed through 3.5 k, holds the timer's GND 10 V below the line conductor that also forms its VCC and the triac's MT1. At power-up the 0.1 µF capacitor, charged through 10 k, holds Trigger low and starts one timing cycle; Reset is tied to VCC. R = 20 MΩ and C = 1.0 µF set the period to 1.1 RC = 22 s. The output drives the triac gate through 1.0 k. Changing R or C changes the delay.

circuits.title: General test circuit for DC parameters
circuits.description: The circuit the DC parameters are measured in. Threshold and Trigger are tied and driven from a source VS through 2.0 k. With VS at or above two thirds of VCC the output is low; at or below one third it is high. While the output is low, Discharge sinks current from VCC through 700 Ω. A switch puts Reset either on VCC or on a source VR: for the reset test the output is set high, VR applied, and current into pin 7 is looked for. A meter reads VO and a load draws ISink or ISource at the output; ICC is measured in the supply lead.

circuits.title: Monostable (one-shot)
circuits.description: A one-shot timed by RA and C. Threshold and Discharge are joined at the RA-C node. A falling edge on Trigger below VCC/3 drives the output high and lets C charge through RA; at 2VCC/3 the output returns low and C is discharged. The high time is 1.1 RA C. The load RL can hang from the output to VCC or to ground. Control is bypassed with 0.01 µF. VCC is 5.0 V to 15 V.
notes: Reset is tied to VCC when it is not used.
Values for the monostable waveforms: RA = 10 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF, RL = 1.0 kΩ, VCC = 15 V.

circuits.title: Astable (free-running oscillator)
circuits.description: A free-running oscillator. C charges through RA and RB from VCC/3 to 2VCC/3 with the output high, then discharges through RB into Discharge with the output low; Trigger and Threshold both watch the RB-C node, so the timer restarts itself every cycle. The high time is 0.695 (RA + RB) C, the low time 0.695 RB C and the frequency 1.44 / ((RA + 2RB) C). The load RL can go to VCC or to ground. VCC is 5.0 V to 15 V.
notes: Values for the astable waveforms: RA = 5.1 kΩ, RB = 3.9 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF, RL = 1.0 kΩ, VCC = 15 V.

circuits.title: Linear voltage sweep
circuits.description: A monostable whose timing resistor is replaced by a constant-current source, so the capacitor voltage rises as a straight ramp. A 2N4403 PNP with RE in its emitter and its base held at VB by the R1-R2 divider feeds I = (VCC - VB - VBE) / RE into C. The ramp runs from 0 to 2VCC/3 in t = 2VCC / (3I) and is taken from the capacitor as the sweep output; Output gives the matching digital pulse. With VB much larger than VBE the ramp time no longer depends on VCC.
notes: Values for the ramp waveforms: RE = 10 kΩ, R1 = 39 kΩ, R2 = 100 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF, VCC = 15 V.

circuits.title: Missing pulse detector
circuits.description: A monostable that is restarted by every input pulse. The input drives Trigger and the base of a 2N4403 PNP whose emitter sits on the timing node, so each low-going input pulse empties C and begins a new period. With the delay set a little longer than the normal pulse spacing the period never ends while pulses keep coming; a missing pulse, or a drop in input frequency, lets it run out and the output changes state.
notes: Values for the detector waveforms: RA = 2.0 kΩ, RL = 1.0 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF, VCC = 15 V.

circuits.title: Pulse width modulator
circuits.description: A monostable triggered by a continuous clock. The modulating signal goes straight into Control, which moves the threshold level and with it the time C needs to charge through RA, so each output pulse is as wide as the modulation voltage asks. VCC is 5.0 V to 15 V.
notes: Values for the modulation waveforms: RA = 10 kΩ, C = 0.02 µF, VCC = 15 V.

circuits.title: Sequential timer
circuits.description: Three monostables in a chain. Each output feeds the next stage's Trigger through 0.001 µF, with 27 k holding that Trigger at VCC, so the falling edge at the end of one period gives the next a short low pulse and starts it. Started from the first Trigger, the first stage runs 10 ms (9.1 k, 1.0 µF), the second 50 ms (9.1 k, 5.0 µF) and the third 18.2 k with 5.0 µF. Each output also drives its own load. VCC is 5.0 V to 15 V.

operation.text: The timing element is an external resistor and capacitor; the chip supplies the rest: a comparator for the trigger input, a comparator for the capacitor voltage, a flip-flop, a discharge transistor and an output stage. Both comparator references come from a divider across the supply (thresholds at VCC/3 and 2VCC/3), so timing does not change with supply voltage. It works as a one-shot or as an oscillator, and times from microseconds to hours.

Threshold and Discharge are tied together on the RC node. When Trigger falls below VCC/3 the flip-flop is set: the discharge transistor turns off and the output goes high, and C charges exponentially through R. At 2VCC/3 the threshold comparator clears the flip-flop, C is discharged and the output goes low. A trigger during the period has no effect until the period is over, and the trigger pulse must be shorter than the period. Figure 16 relates R, C and the delay.

Pulling Reset low turns the discharge transistor on, empties the capacitor and keeps it from charging, which stops a timing cycle. The output does not change while the reset voltage is applied. Reset should go to VCC when unused. The reset threshold is 0.4 V to 1.0 V (0.7 V typical).

Trigger and Threshold are both tied to the capacitor, so the timer retriggers itself and the capacitor swings between VCC/3 and 2VCC/3, charging through RA plus RB and discharging through RB alone. The ratio of RA to RB sets the duty cycle, and the charge and discharge times do not depend on VCC. For the highest duty cycle RA is made as small as the 200 mA discharge-current rating allows.
The threshold input current limits the largest timing resistance: at 15 V, RA + RB may total at most 20 MΩ.
Used as a one-shot with a constant-current source in place of the timing resistor, the timer charges C linearly from 0 to 2VCC/3, giving a voltage ramp.

Setting the delay slightly longer than the spacing of the incoming pulses keeps the timer restarting; the cycle completes, and the output changes, only when a pulse is missing or the frequency changes.
With the timer in monostable mode and triggered by a steady pulse train, a signal on Control (pin 5) shifts the threshold and so the capacitor charge time, modulating the output pulse width.
Timers can trigger one another in a chain. Started by a trigger, the first stage runs 10 ms; at its end its output drops low briefly and starts the second, which runs 50 ms, and so on.

In the general test circuit the output is low with VS at or above 2/3 VCC and high with VS at or below 1/3 VCC. With the output low, pin 7 sinks current. Reset is tested by setting the output high, applying the reset voltage and checking for current into pin 7. Reset is tied to VCC when it is not in use.
Up to 200 mA flows in either direction at the output, which drives TTL loads and may be wired to be on or off at rest. Timing drifts by about 0.005 % per °C.
